answer: Each identity registers a mesa beacon post with an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files a beacon log to the sonnet ledger: ripple spacing, wind speed, serial, saffron seal. An auditor recomputes ripple spacing from the mesa table, checks the sonnet ledger and saffron seal, and burns the bond on over-3-percent error, reused serial, or copied log. First filing 36; kth 36+6(k-1); 1000th 6030; 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000, 80,000 locked. A rented-beacon ring fails: one post cannot serve two keys, and copied spacing fails checks. Honest identities pay 36 once, recovered after a clean epoch.
